name: How to Paint Bathroom Walls After a Leak or Moisture Repair

step.name: Step 1: Verify the moisture problem is solved and surfaces are dry. Never apply paint over damp drywall or an unresolved leak. Check that framing and drywall patches have fully dried out, and clean any surface mildew with an appropriate cleaner before coating, as advised by EPA guidelines.
step.text: Step 1: Verify the moisture problem is solved and surfaces are dry. Never apply paint over damp drywall or an unresolved leak. Check that framing and drywall patches have fully dried out, and clean any surface mildew with an appropriate cleaner before coating, as advised by EPA guidelines.

step.name: Step 2: Scrape loose, flaking paint and sand transitions. Use a sturdy putty knife to remove loose edges around past moisture blisters. Sand the borders where sound paint meets bare drywall with medium-grit sandpaper to feather the edge flat, ensuring no sharp ridges remain visible.

step.name: Step 3: Clean and degrease the walls thoroughly. Bathroom walls collect soap film, shampoo haze, and hair products that break paint adhesion. Wash down the walls with a mild cleaner, rinse completely with clean water, and allow the surfaces to dry completely under active ventilation.
step.text: Step 3: Clean and degrease the walls thoroughly. Bathroom walls collect soap film, shampoo haze, and hair products that break paint adhesion. Wash down the walls with a mild cleaner, rinse completely with clean water, and allow the surfaces to dry completely under active ventilation.

step.name: Step 4: Spot-prime bare drywall and repair patches. Technical data sheets for products like Benjamin Moore Bath & Spa mandate spot-priming repairs before topcoating. Apply a high-adhesion, moisture-sealing primer over all exposed gypsum, compound patches, and stained spots to lock the surface against humidity.

Apply a high-adhesion, moisture-sealing primer over all exposed gypsum, compound patches, and stained spots to lock the surface against humidity.

step.name: Step 5: Cut in corners and roll the first finish coat. Use a quality synthetic brush to cut clean lines along the ceiling and trim, then use a short-nap roller to apply the specialized bathroom paint evenly. Keep a wet edge and run an exhaust fan or window vent to assist drying without blowing dust onto wet walls.

step.name: Step 6: Allow proper recoat time and apply the second coat. Let the initial coat dry for the manufacturer's specified window—often several hours depending on room humidity. Roll your second uniform coat, and keep showers off for at least 24 hours to let the resin network fully cure.
